extraction.document_summary: AIA Life Dividends is a whole life protection plan for a child (or yourself) that combines lifetime protection with annual dividends. It provides coverage for death and Total and Permanent Disability (TPD): death coverage ceases at age 100 and TPD ceases at age 70. Premiums for the base plan are paid for 10 years, while protection continues up to 100. Annual dividends are non-guaranteed and are received at the end of the 5th policy year, with options to withdraw in cash, accumulate interest, or use dividends to reduce premiums—without affecting the coverage amount and terminal dividends. The brochure also describes non-guaranteed terminal dividends payable on surrender, claim, or maturity. Riders can be added for critical illnesses and premium waiver, including CCA/ECCA and Early Critical Protector Payor Benefit (II), with rider coverage ending at age 100 and rider premiums payable up to age 65 or 10 years (whichever is longer).
quality_notes: Brochure clearly states core base coverage (death and TPD) and key dividend mechanics (annual dividends at end of 5th year, terminal dividends).
Rider names and broad covered critical-illness coverage counts are provided, but detailed benefit amounts are largely only illustrated in examples (not stated as generally available plan limits).
Some important fields (e.g., underwriting type, eligibility ages, exact payout formula for critical illness riders) are not explicitly stated.

policies.quick_summary: Whole life protection with non-guaranteed annual dividends payable from the end of the 5th policy year, plus optional critical-illness and premium-coverage acceleration/waiver riders (CCA/ECCA/ECPPB (II)). Base plan pays premiums for 10 years with protection up to age 100 (death) and age 70 (TPD). Annual dividends can be withdrawn/accumulated/reinvested into premium reduction without affecting coverage amount and terminal dividends; terminal dividends are one-time and non-guaranteed upon surrender/claim/maturity/certain events as described in the notes section of the brochure examples/notes footprint.

riders.name: Critical Cover Accelerator (CCA) rider
riders.description: A critical illness rider providing coverage for major stage critical illnesses (brochure states number of major stage critical illnesses).
riders.coverage_term_description: Coverage for CCA rider will cease at age 100; premiums are payable up to age 65 or 10 years, whichever is longer.
riders.premium_payment_term_description: Payable up to age 65 or 10 years, whichever is longer.
riders.notes: Brochure also explains that in an illustration, a CCA claim may partially accelerate the AIA Life Dividends coverage amount and can partially pay out terminal dividends; details are example-based.

riders.name: Early Critical Protector Payor Benefit (II) (ECPPB (II)) rider
riders.description: A rider that can provide premium-waiver protection for the base plan and/or ECCA premium in the illustration when an early critical illness (e.g., Carcinoma-in-situ) occurs.
riders.notes: The brochure provides an illustration: ECPPB (II) waives the AIA Life Dividends annual premium for 5 years and also the ECCA rider annual premium until the child reaches age 25. The brochure does not state general duration rules outside this example.
